problems.title: An integer above a reciprocal
problems.question: Find the least positive integer greater than the reciprocal of 0.111.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: 1000/111=9+1/111, which is just above 9. The next integer is 10.

problems.question: Find the largest two-digit number that is a sum of four consecutive positive integers.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: Such sums are 2 modulo 4. The largest below 100 is 98, achieved by 23+24+25+26.

problems.title: A right-triangle median equals a leg
problems.question: C is the right angle, CO is a median, CO=CB and AB=12. Find AC.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: The median to a hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse; $AC^2+CB^2=AB^2$.

problems.title: A trapezoid height from an inclined side
problems.question: Trapezoid bases AD=15,BC=9, side CD=6, angle ADC=30°. Find area.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: The height is 3 and area=(15+9)×3/2=36.

problems.title: Compare mean, median and mode
problems.question: Scores are 15,23,15. Which listed relationship is true?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: Mean = sum/count; median = middle sorted value; mode = most frequent.
steps: Sorted scores are 15,15,23. Median and mode both equal 15, whereas mean is 53/3>15.

problems.title: Average speed for an out-and-back trip
problems.question: A distance-time graph rises from 0 to 3 km at 50 minutes, then returns to 0 at 80 minutes. Find average speed.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: Average speed = total distance/total elapsed time.
steps: The tourist travels 3+3=6 km in 80/60=4/3 hours. Average speed=6/(4/3)=4.5 km/h.

problems.title: Count codes with digit-sum constraints
problems.question: A four-digit code has first-two-digit sum 17 and last-two-digit sum 5. Count all codes.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: Multiply independent counts for the ordered pairs.
steps: The first pair is (8,9) or (9,8), giving 2 choices. The last pair is (0,5),(1,4),…,(5,0), giving 6 choices. Total=12.

problems.title: Vertices of a prism
problems.question: A prism has 30 edges. How many vertices?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has $3n$ edges and $2n$ vertices.
steps: 3n=30 gives n=10, so it has 20 vertices.

problems.title: Rotate a triangle about each of its sides
problems.question: Rotation about any of a triangle’s three sides produces a union of two cones. What must the triangle be?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: A double cone is produced when the perpendicular foot from the opposite vertex is strictly inside the side.
steps: This requires both endpoint angles of each chosen side to be acute. Requiring this for all three sides forces all three angles to be acute.
Conversely, all three altitudes of an acute triangle meet the interiors of the opposite sides, giving two nondegenerate cones in each rotation.

problems.title: An equation true for every x
problems.question: When does ax=b have infinitely many real solutions?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: A nonzero coefficient gives a unique solution; zero coefficient needs a zero right side.
steps: For a=0,b=0 the equation is 0=0 for every real x. If a=0,b≠0 it has no solution.

problems.title: An absolute-value equation with no solution
problems.question: Find k for which |x|=−k²+3k+4 has no real solution.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: The right side must be negative; $-k^2+3k+4=-(k-4)(k+1)$.
steps: No solution occurs when (k−4)(k+1)>0, or k<−1 or k>4. The endpoints each give the solution x=0 and must be excluded.

problems.title: Opposite faces using three die views
problems.question: The three views show (top,front,right)=(2,1,3),(1,4,5),(4,6,5). What is opposite 3?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: A rigid rotation preserves adjacency and cyclic orientation of three faces at a corner.
steps: Use the first view as reference: top=2, front=1, right=3. In the second view top becomes 1. The oriented positions of its front 4 and right 5 place 4 opposite the original right 3 and 5 opposite top 2.
The remaining pair is 1 opposite 6. The third view (top 4,front 6,right 5) confirms this orientation.

problems.title: Only odd-index terms contribute
problems.question: cₖ=0 for even k and cₖ=k for odd k. Find the first 100 terms’ sum.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: The first m positive odd integers sum to $m^2$.
steps: The nonzero terms are 1+3+…+99, exactly 50 odd integers. Their sum is 50²=2500.

problems.title: A median change does not fix the mean change
problems.question: One of nine data values changes and the median rises by 10. How much does the mean rise?
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: Mean change = changed-value increment/9; a median change does not determine that increment.
steps: Example data: 0,0,0,0,0,10,20,30,40 have median 0. Change one zero to 10: median becomes 10 and mean rises 10/9.
Instead change one zero to 20: median still becomes 10, but mean rises 20/9. These give different answers with the same median change.

problems.title: Match a trigonometric identity for every input

problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: Matching the sine phase for every x gives α=π/4 modulo 2π. Only π/4 lies in the stated interval.

problems.title: Distance across perpendicular planes
problems.question: Planes α,β are perpendicular and meet along p. A∈α,B∈β are distances a,b from p; their projections on p are distance c apart. Find AB.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: The three perpendicular displacement components have magnitudes a,b,c.
steps: Take p as the z-axis, α as the xz-plane and β as the yz-plane. A=(±a,0,z₁), B=(0,±b,z₂), with |z₁−z₂|=c.
Pythagoras in space gives AB²=a²+b²+c².

problems.title: Distance between two tips of a pyramid net
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has volume 8,height 3. In its flat cross-shaped net A and B are tips on adjacent lateral triangles. Find AB.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: s²=8, so s=2√2 and l=√(9+2)=√11. Place the square at [0,s]×[0,s].
The left tip is A=(−l,s/2) and the top tip B=(s/2,s+l). Each coordinate difference is l+s/2=√11+√2.

problems.title: Two pipes used for different lengths of time
problems.question: The first pipe alone fills a tank six hours faster than the second. Both run five hours; then only the second runs three more hours. Find the time if both run throughout.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: If solo times are t and t+6, the filled fraction is $5/t+8/(t+6)=1$.
steps: Multiply by t(t+6): 5(t+6)+8t=t²+6t, giving t²−7t−30=0. The positive solution is t=10; the other pipe takes 16 hours.
Combined rate=1/10+1/16=13/80 tanks/hour, so combined filling time is 80/13 hours.

problems.title: One shaded corner beside an inscribed circle
problems.question: A circle of radius √2 touches both radii and the arc of a 90° sector. Find the shaded upper-left region in the picture.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
formulas: The circle centre is (r,r), so sector radius $R=r\sqrt2+r=2+\sqrt2$.
steps: The area of the sector outside the circle is πR²/4−πr²=(√2−1/2)π.
This outside area has three components: the small corner at the sector centre and two congruent side regions. The corner is a square of side r minus a quarter-circle of radius r: r²−πr²/4=2−π/2.
Subtract that corner from the outside area and divide by two. The shaded side region is [(√2−1/2)π−(2−π/2)]/2=π/√2−1.

problems.title: When two closed half-planes do not meet
problems.question: Find conditions on a,b for (2a−3)x+3y≤3b and 3x−2y≤5−9b to have no solution.
problems.idea: Choose a formula from the data and check that the result fits the original question.
steps: If the boundary slopes differ, the lines intersect, and their intersection satisfies both non-strict inequalities. Thus emptiness requires equal slopes.
Set −(2a−3)/3=3/2, giving a=−3/4. The lower bound then lies strictly above the upper bound iff (9b−5)/2>b, or b>5/7.
Equality b=5/7 leaves the common boundary line and is not empty.
